C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-2-D4F54467.IntentSummary:
**This T2 plan converts the approved `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-2-D4F54467` spec into four sequential tasks plus the close.** The durable modules are exactly `M-CLI`, `M-CURSOR`, and `M-GATES`; the verification anchors are their `V-M-*` entries. `ObservedWriteScope` is the spec's nine forced paths (`src/grace-generate.ts`, `src/grace-cursor.ts`, `src/gates/ledger.ts`, `src/grace-generate.test.ts`, `src/grace-cursor.test.ts`, `src/grace-supersede.test.ts`, `.github/workflows/validate.yml`, `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`, `README.md`), with no globs, **plus** the predecessor's archive arrival that the already-run `ngrace supersede` wrote (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-1-DE5A1A05/{spec,plan,design-context}.xml`): the successor's recorded base `dc549ed` predates the supersede move committed at `9bdf72e`, so those foreign-bundle artifacts otherwise register as out-of-scope and the review reddens. The plan still lists no bundle-own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, `design-context.xml`, `run/`, `run.xml`, or `run-ledger.xml` path; the close writes no record file because this bundle pays no finding, so no `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/` path is in scope. Those three predecessor-archive entries are **accounting only**: no task and no close writes them, and a guard in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` compares each file's bytes to its SHA-256 as committed at `9bdf72e12b4542f497dca1d00408783cf119da57`, so an accidental archive edit reddens `bun run validate:ci`.
**Execution is sequential: T-001 → T-002 → T-003 → T-004.** T-001 binds candidate-lock identity to a handle pinned to the observed lock in `src/grace-cursor.ts` and extends `src/grace-cursor.test.ts` with the recycled-identity discriminator, the pre-pin `b53d13df47cdf8d85f75b33502c6ecd9e97ff262` control, and the timeout diagnostic. T-002 binds candidate-directory identity to a handle pinned to the acquired directory in `src/grace-generate.ts`, makes acquisition fail-closed, exports the idempotent `releaseAcquiredCandidate` API, closes the pin exactly once in `cleanupCandidate`, and extends `src/grace-generate.test.ts` with the distinct/recycled cleanup probes, the ordinary-success and forced-failure directions, the release semantics, the returned-published-record same-path-replacement probe, and the descriptor-lifetime relation driven over both acquire→publish→release and post-open-failure cycles. T-003 routes the release owners: `writeSpecNew` is exported with an optional `CandidateIo` seam and closes its successful record before returning, the implicit supersede transaction in `src/gates/ledger.ts` closes its minted record before returning on success and lets `cleanupCandidate` close it on failure, and the `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API` / `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE` owner tests land in `src/grace-generate.test.ts` and `src/grace-supersede.test.ts`. The writer owner is proven **platform-agnostically** with a real captured handle (`AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: successful writeSpecNew closes its record before returning`), while the in-process repeated-call `/proc/self/fd` relation stays a separate Linux-only `itLinux` test. T-004 restores full history to the `validate` checkout, adds the two Windows filtered invocations and their guards in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`, and lands the `README.md` sentence; it is the only task that carries `Satisfies`.
**Criterion mapping.** All fourteen close-bound criteria (`AC-CLEANUP-PINNED-DISTINCT`, `AC-CLEANUP-PINNED-RECYCLED`, `AC-RECLAIM-PINNED-DISTINCT`, `AC-RECLAIM-PINNED-RECYCLED`, `AC-RECLAIM-TIMEOUT-DIAGNOSTIC`, `AC-PIN-SUCCESS-AND-REFUSAL`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API`, `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-NO-LEAK`, `AC-README-REFUSAL`, `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY`, `AC-BASELINE-CONTROL-AVAILABLE`, `AC-CLOSE-LINT`, `AC-CLOSE-SUITE`) are evaluated by the close's `CloseEvidence` commands and are deliberately absent from every `Satisfies`. The single ordinary criterion, `AC-WINDOWS-DIRECTORY-PIN`, is mapped exactly once, to T-004.
**Windows evidence sequence (owned by the implementation authority and the user, never invoked here).** The implementation authority independently validates the implementation and creates the pre-Windows candidate/lifecycle commit on `c-supersede-membership`, reporting its full SHA, without marking T-004 complete; the user pushes that commit. The external executor takes no remote action, and neither party invokes a remote action on the executor's behalf. The PR's `windows-compatibility` job then runs the two filtered invocations, each naming its directions one by one (the `src/grace-generate.test.ts` pin criteria, the platform-agnostic writer owner, the publish-failure owner, and the Windows-only directory test; the `src/grace-supersede.test.ts` four `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE` owners). Execution pauses at that job. The evidence is that job's Actions outcome for the exact pushed candidate head SHA; a failed run, an absent run, or a run at a different SHA leaves `AC-WINDOWS-DIRECTORY-PIN` unmet and blocks the close. The old green Windows check on the pre-repair SHA is never evidence for the new code. If the Windows failure proves the approved handle mechanism cannot meet ordinary success, the authority stops for review rather than amending the approved spec or shipping a limitation.
**The full CI-equivalent verification is the single `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` `bun run validate:ci`, run at the close under `--assertions final --run-commands`; it is not duplicated as a per-task command.**

T-001.Title: Pin reclaim identity to the observed lock handle

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In `src/grace-cursor.ts`, `observeCandidateLock` opens the lock, reads the ownership bytes from that handle, and records `dev`/`ino` with `fstatSync` of that handle; it returns the handle with the observation. `reclaimCandidateLock` compares the current path's bytes and `dev`/`ino` to the pinned observation and closes the handle exactly once after the decision on every branch (match, mismatch, `ENOENT`, or throw). `acquireCandidateLock` closes the observation handle on the live-holder wait path so repeated waits do not accumulate open descriptors. The two phases are distinct and both required. **Phase 1, observation:** the pinned bytes and pair come exclusively from the opened handle — no `readFileSync(path)` or `statSync(path)` supplies the pinned bytes or pair. **Phase 2, immediate pre-unlink revalidation:** `reclaimCandidateLock` reads the current **path** bytes and stats the current **path** and compares both to the pinned pair; the pinned handle keeps the observed inode allocated, so the path comparison is sound. The dead-holder reclaim test drives the matching-owner path; the different-token B/A/B and same-bytes replacement tests drive mismatch paths and preserve the replacement bytes.

`src/grace-cursor.test.ts` keeps and passes the existing different-token controls on the real exported boundary with recursive byte snapshots: the B/A/B control `AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE: a stale observer cannot unlink a replacement holder (B/A/B)`, the mismatched-token release no-op, the own-lock removal after A releases, and the successor-lock preservation control.

The same-bytes test `AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE: a same-bytes replacement inode is not unlinked` probes the filesystem for inode recycling and reports both the observed and recreated pairs. On a recycling filesystem it asserts the pin forces the recreated inode to differ and that B refuses while the replacement bytes and inode survive; on a non-recycling filesystem it emits a named skip reason and does not claim the discriminating case.

A new pre-pin control `AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE pre-pin control: b53d13d unlinks the recycled replacement` adds a disposable `git worktree` at the full hash `b53d13df47cdf8d85f75b33502c6ecd9e97ff262`, and on a recycling filesystem drives the same fixture against that pre-pin module and asserts the replacement is unlinked and B acquires; on a non-recycling filesystem it skips with the named reason. The control is removed in a `finally`.

A new test `AC-CANDIDATE-RECLAIM-EXCLUSIVE timeout diagnostic: running child, signal, stderr and markers` forces the bounded wait to expire and asserts the failure names whether the child is still running (reporting `running`) or has exited (reporting the numeric exit code, or the signal after a bounded kill and await), the stderr tail, and the marker states, and always terminates and reaps the child before the test ends.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "a stale observer cannot unlink a replacement holder"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "reclaims a dead fresh holder immediately"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "a same-bytes replacement inode is not unlinked"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "pre-pin control"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "timeout diagnostic"

T-002.Title: Pin candidate-directory identity, fail-closed acquisition, and the release capability

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In `src/grace-generate.ts`, `AcquiredCandidate` carries the acquired directory handle and a released flag. `acquireCandidate` opens the candidate directory first, records `dev`/`ino` with `fstatSync` of that handle, and stores the handle; `cleanupCandidateLocked` compares the current path pair to the pinned pair immediately before the destructive phase and closes the handle exactly once on every return path. On a platform that cannot remove the directory while the handle is open, the handle is closed only after every ownership check and immediately before the destructive call, inside the spec's post-validation/pre-unlink boundary.

Acquisition is fail-closed. If the open or the `fstat` fails, `acquireCandidate` refuses with a diagnostic naming the preserved candidate; the CLI exits non-zero, the candidate is byte-identical to its post-`mkdir`, pre-open snapshot, and no `spec.xml` is treated as published. The unpinned `dev`/`ino` comparison is never used as a substitute. The `CandidateIo` seam carries `openSync`, `fstatSync`, and `closeSync`, so a real handle can be allocated and a post-open `fstat` failure injected; the failure path closes the handle exactly once.

`releaseAcquiredCandidate(candidate)` is exported from `src/grace-generate.ts`, closes the pin exactly once, and a second call is a safe no-op. `cleanupCandidate` closes the pin exactly once on every return path, success or refusal, and a returned record is never silently invalidated. `cleanupCandidate` on an already-released record returns `removed === false` with a diagnostic naming the record as released and preserves every byte; it never falls back to the unpinned comparison. The new exported symbol is added to the `START_MODULE_MAP` exports of `src/grace-generate.ts` so the MODULE_MAP/EXPORTS parity check stays green.

`src/grace-generate.test.ts` drives the directory-pin directions on every supported platform. The ordinary-success direction asserts a real mint pins the directory and a handled cleanup removes the owned directory; the forced-failure direction injects a real `openSync` (or `fstat`) failure through the `CandidateIo` seam and asserts the operation refuses with the candidate preserved and a named diagnostic. It also carries the distinct-identity cleanup probe, the recycled-identity cleanup probe against `b53d13df47cdf8d85f75b33502c6ecd9e97ff262`, the release-semantics probe, a non-vacuous returned-record probe, and a descriptor-lifetime probe. The returned-record probe returns a **published** record from `mintResolvedBundle`, replaces its directory at the same path (writing the replacement's own `spec.xml` bytes), passes that returned record to `cleanupCandidate`, and asserts the held pin detects the replacement — the refusal is the identity comparison, not the released-or-absent path — while the replacement and its bytes survive. This proves the pin was still held at cleanup time and was not silently invalidated by return; the hand-built `mkCandidate` (c) probe cannot and is not the evidence. The descriptor-lifetime probe drives repeated acquire→publish→release cycles **and** repeated acquire→fail→cleanup cycles in which `openSync` succeeds and allocates the real handle and `fstatSync` fails after the open; it asserts that the post-open failure path closes the handle (the captured descriptor no longer resolves) and that on Linux the `/proc/self/fd` count returns to baseline and does not grow with the cycle count. It runs as `process.platform === "linux" ? it : it.skip` and skips with a named reason elsewhere. Test titles: `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED pre-pin control: b53d13d deletes the recycled replacement`, `AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: an ordinary mint pins the candidate and cleanup removes it`, `AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: a forced open failure preserves the candidate and refuses`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE: releaseAcquiredCandidate closes once; cleanup after release refuses`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-NO-LEAK: a returned published candidate detects a same-path replacement`, and `AC-PIN-RELEASE-LIFETIME: descriptor count does not grow over cycles`. The existing hand-constructed `AcquiredCandidate` helpers in `src/grace-generate.test.ts` (`ownedCandidate` and the foreign-marker-token fixture) open the pin when they build the record, so the unchanged `AC-CLEANUP-LOCK-API` and `AC-CLEANUP-VALIDATE-FIRST` tests keep exercising removal and validate-first with a pinned record rather than the released-or-absent refusal.

bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "pre-pin control"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "an ordinary mint pins the candidate and cleanup removes it"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "a forced open failure preserves the candidate and refuses"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "releaseAcquiredCandidate closes once"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "a returned published candidate detects a same-path replacement"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "descriptor count does not grow over cycles"

T-003.Title: Route the release owners in grace-generate and the supersede transaction

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `writeSpecNew` in `src/grace-generate.ts` closes its successful record before returning: it captures the `publishSpecNew` result and calls `releaseAcquiredCandidate` on the returned record, so an in-process series of repeated successful `spec new` calls leaves the process descriptor count flat rather than leaking one handle per mint. `publishSpecNew` keeps closing on its failure path through `cleanupCandidate`; closure is exactly once on every branch. `writeSpecNew` is **exported** with an optional `CandidateIo` parameter and threads that seam into both `publishSpecNew` and `releaseAcquiredCandidate`, and `releaseAcquiredCandidate` accepts the same optional seam so its close routes through `io.closeSync` when supplied; the new export is added to the `START_MODULE_MAP` of `src/grace-generate.ts` so the MODULE_MAP/EXPORTS parity check stays green. This narrow seam is what lets the writer owner be driven with a real captured handle on every platform.

The implicit-mint supersede transaction in `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`supersedeChangeBundle`) imports and calls `releaseAcquiredCandidate` on the minted record after the successful rename, before returning; on a post-mint failure it keeps calling `cleanupCandidate` exactly once (removal and refusal/residue both close the descriptor), and a pre-publication mint failure closes internally through the inner publisher with no returned record reaching the outer cleanup. No branch double-closes. The `supersedeChangeBundle` I/O seam forwards `closeSync` (beside `unlinkSync`/`rmdirSync`) to `cleanupCandidate`, so the owner tests count the close through the production seam rather than inferring it.

`src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains the non-transaction owner tests under the `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API` title prefix. **The platform-agnostic writer owner** `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: successful writeSpecNew closes its record before returning` is a plain `it(...)` (never `itLinux`/`it.skip`) that calls the exported `writeSpecNew` with a `CandidateIo` capturing `openSync`/`closeSync`, asserts the captured descriptor no longer resolves via `fstatSync` after the in-process boundary, and counts exactly one `closeSync`; it therefore executes on Windows as well as Linux. **The Linux long-cycle relation** `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: repeated spec new leaves the writer's handle count flat` stays a separate `itLinux` test that drives an in-process `specCommand.subCommands.new.run` series and asserts the `/proc/self/fd` relation, skipped with the named reason off Linux. `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: a publish failure closes the pin exactly once` injects a real `spec.xml` write failure, asserts the captured descriptor no longer resolves, and counts exactly one `closeSync`. Every direction uses real handles, not a source regex. The existing `AC-WRAPPER-ROUTES: mintBundle and mintResolvedBundle converge on publishSpecNew via writeSpecNew` source-shape assertion is updated to the new `writeSpecNew` body (capture, `releaseAcquiredCandidate`, return) so the wrapper-route guard stays green.

`src/grace-supersede.test.ts` gains the transaction owner tests under the `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE` title prefix, driven with real captured descriptors: `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a successful implicit mint closes the transaction's pin` (captured `dirFd` no longer resolves after the transaction returns), `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint failure removal closes the pin exactly once` (cleanup outcome `removed === true`, exactly one `closeSync`, descriptor closed), `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint refusal/residue closes the pin exactly once` (foreign entry preserved, `removed === false`, exactly one `closeSync`, descriptor closed), and `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a pre-publication mint failure closes internally without a returned record` (inner cleanup observed once, outer cleanup observed zero). The tests keep the archived post-validation/pre-unlink boundary and add no new one.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "successful writeSpecNew closes its record"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "repeated spec new leaves the writer's handle count flat"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "a publish failure closes the pin exactly once"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-supersede.test.ts -t "AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-supersede.test.ts -t "a real inner mint failure after exclusive acquisition cleans up once"

T-004.Title: Full-history checkout, Windows regression catch, guards, and the README refusal

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `.github/workflows/validate.yml` declares `fetch-depth: 0` on the `validate` job's checkout step, so `git worktree add --detach ... 6dd1d95` resolves in a pull-request checkout and the isolated `AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE` baseline control runs.

The `windows-compatibility` job carries **two** dedicated filtered invocation steps, and neither adds a whole test file. The first, `bun run test src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: an ordinary mint|AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: a forced open failure|AC-PIN-RELEASE: releaseAcquiredCandidate|AC-PIN-RELEASE-NO-LEAK|AC-PIN-RELEASE-LIFETIME|AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: successful writeSpecNew closes its record|AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: a publish failure closes the pin exactly once|AC-WINDOWS-DIRECTORY-PIN"`, names each platform-agnostic pin/release owner direction individually, including the executed platform-agnostic writer owner and the publish-failure owner, plus the Windows-only directory test; the Linux-only `/proc/self/fd` writer relation is deliberately not selected there. The second, `bun run test src/grace-supersede.test.ts -t "AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a successful implicit mint|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint failure removal|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint refusal/residue|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a pre-publication mint failure"`, names each of the four implicit-supersede owner tests. Each invocation must select and execute a nonzero count; bun refuses a `-t` selector that matches zero tests, and the guards below keep every named direction present. The `src/grace-generate.test.ts` file is **not** added whole (its unconditional historical-baseline and competitor-interceptor tests have unrelated Windows assumptions), and the whole existing `src/grace-supersede.test.ts` is **not** added (its other tests spawn `bun`/`git`, toggle `chmod`, and copy/readlink fixtures).

The Windows-conditional test uses the required form `process.platform === "win32" ? it : it.skip` and `AC-WINDOWS-DIRECTORY-PIN: candidate pin success and cleanup removal` drives an ordinary mint with the pin, a handled cleanup that removes the owned directory (or closes the handle only at the last ownership check), and the forced-acquisition-failure refusal with preserved bytes. The platform-agnostic writer owner runs on Windows; only the Linux `/proc/self/fd` long-cycle relation (`itLinux`) and the Windows-only directory test are permitted to skip off their platform. A Windows run in which the writer owner skips is a failure, not a pass.

`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` gains `windowsPinInvocation(xml)` (extended) and `windowsSupersedeInvocation(xml)`, each reading its own `windows-compatibility` job `run:` line that names `src/grace-generate.test.ts` and `src/grace-supersede.test.ts` respectively, plus guards that fail when either invocation drops any required direction. The pin guard requires, one per direction, `AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: an ordinary mint`, `AC-PIN-ACQUISITION: a forced open failure`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE: releaseAcquiredCandidate`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-NO-LEAK`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-LIFETIME`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: successful writeSpecNew closes its record`, `AC-PIN-RELEASE-API: a publish failure closes the pin exactly once`, and `AC-WINDOWS-DIRECTORY-PIN`; the supersede guard requires, one per direction, `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a successful implicit mint`, `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint failure removal`, `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint refusal/residue`, and `AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a pre-publication mint failure`. A family prefix alone cannot satisfy either guard, so a retained prefix cannot mask a missing or skipped owner test. A further guard reads `src/grace-generate.test.ts` and fails when the writer owner is declared with `itLinux`/`it.skip` instead of a plain `it(...)`. The Ubuntu `validate` job keeps `fetch-depth: 0` and its `validateJobCheckoutDepth` guard; the Windows checkout does not need full history under this variant.

`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` gains a byte guard over the predecessor's archive arrival: `PREDECESSOR_ARCHIVE_SHA256` pins the SHA-256 of `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-1-DE5A1A05/{spec,plan,design-context}.xml` as committed at `9bdf72e12b4542f497dca1d00408783cf119da57`, and the guard fails on any mutation of those bytes. The three `ObservedWriteScope` entries exist to reconcile the recorded-base diff only; **no task and no close writes those archived files**, and the guard reddens `bun run validate:ci` if they change. No archive glob is added.

**T-004 cannot be marked complete until the `windows-compatibility` job succeeds for the exact candidate head SHA.** The implementation authority (not the external executor) validates the implementation and creates the pre-Windows candidate/lifecycle commit without marking T-004 complete; the user pushes it; the authority records the job URL, its conclusion, and the pushed head SHA in the bundle's evidence. A failed run, an absent run, or a run at a different SHA blocks the criterion and the close. The historical green Windows job on the pre-repair SHA is not proof for the new code. If the Windows job shows the approved handle mechanism cannot meet ordinary success, T-004 stops for authority review rather than shipping a limitation.

`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` gains a guard that reads the `validate` job's own checkout step and fails when the depth is not full, keyed on the job's step and never on the file's bytes as a whole, so a reverted depth reddens without a Linux runner; and a guard that asserts `README.md` contains the operator-visible sentence `never delete a candidate whose identity they cannot prove`.

`README.md` carries the spec's operator-visible sentence: *"When the engine cannot pin the identity of a candidate it just created — for example, because the platform refuses to open the candidate directory — `ngrace spec new` and candidate cleanup refuse and leave the candidate in place, naming the preserved path in the diagnostic; they never delete a candidate whose identity they cannot prove."* No other README sentence is required to change.

bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-supersede.test.ts -t "AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a successful implicit mint|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint failure removal|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a post-mint refusal/residue|AC-SUPERSEDE-PIN-RELEASE: a pre-publication mint failure"
